course_name_original: Técnicas de Expresión Oral y Escrita en Inglés
course_name_en: Oral and Written Expression Techniques in English
prerequisites: Prior knowledge of English grammatical and linguistic structures
Communicative competence level B2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages

learning_outcomes.text: Follow and deliver simple oral presentations, making correct use of intonation and expressive possibilities.
Request and offer services related to the work environment, using varied, precise, and appropriate vocabulary for the situation in question.
Participate in meetings and seminars by taking notes, expressing own ideas, and making proposals.
Address routine requests for goods or services over the phone.
Draft and understand formal reports and common professional correspondence according to established rhetorical, grammatical, and lexical norms.

syllabus_topics: Preparation of technical reports: structure and linguistic characteristics
Participating in socio-professional activities within the company context:
Conducting job interviews and presenting CVs
Participating in debates, meetings, and negotiations
Use of language and linguistic signaling techniques
Use of visual aids and body language
Use of voice: rhythm and emphasis

assessment_methods.method: Partial exam (E1): Written individual exam on a cover letter
Practical assignment (T1): Submission of individual *Curriculum Vitae*
Partial exam (E2): Oral individual exam on a simulated job interview
Practical assignment (T2): Submission of a technical report prepared jointly by two or more students
Partial exam (E3): Written exam on the technical report, evaluating linguistic and content aspects individually
Partial exam (E4): Group debate participation evaluated individually
Partial exam (E5): Individual oral presentation on a technological innovation topic
Class participation (C1): Active participation in practical sessions

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as the sum of E1 + T1 + E2 + T2 + E3 + E4 + E5 + E6 + C1. A minimum score of 5 is required to pass the subject. There is no minimum score for individual components. For class participation (C1), students must have a minimum attendance of 80% to practical sessions to be eligible for a grade in this section. For extraordinary calls, students will take a theoretical exam (P1+P2+P3+P4, total 60%) and a practical assignment (T1, 40%). No grades from the ordinary call will be carried over.
